findings.claim: Task 4's test cannot pass from task 4 work alone, and the README tells the learner the opposite. TASK 4 (starter/src/hooks/use-fetch.js line 4) requires the hook to call fetchJson from ../api.js. In the starter (api.js lines 12-15), fetchJson returns response.json() for every status, and the hook never sees the status. So tests/t4-use-fetch-hook.test.jsx lines 43-45, which expect error.message 'HTTP 500', fail until TASK 5 part 1 (the response.ok check in api.js) is also done. The failure shows only 'expected null not to be null' under the comment 'A non-2xx response becomes an error, not data', which points at the hook rather than api.js. The 404 banner check in t3 (lines 40-49) has the same hidden dependency. README line 46-49 discloses only the test 1 coupling. Troubleshooting line 133 ('Task 4 tests pass but task 5 still fails') describes a state the learner cannot reach with an unfixed fetchJson.
findings.recommendation: Move the response.ok check into the task that first needs it: make 'fetchJson throws HTTP <status>' part of task 4 (or a task before it), and keep task 5 about the four overview screens. Alternatively, state the coupling explicitly in 'How to test' and in the TASK 4 comment. Rewrite the troubleshooting entry so it matches the real order.

findings.claim: The task order does not match the dependencies. Task 3 (the detail page) must 'load the service with your hook from task 4' (README lines 88-90, ServiceDetailPage.jsx line 5), so a learner who works top to bottom reaches task 3 while useFetch is still the stub that returns {data: null, loading: false, error: null}. The stub can only produce a broken or empty page. t3 also needs task 5 part 1 for its 404 banner (see the previous finding). Unlike part 1, this README never says to work in order and never names this coupling.
findings.recommendation: Put the hook before the detail page (renumber so useFetch plus the fetchJson ok check is task 3 and the detail page is task 4), or tell learners to do task 4 before task 3. Then update the coupling note at line 46-49 to list every cross-task dependency.

findings.claim: The partial-objective note lists only navigation#o2's replace clause and loading-data-with-useeffect#o3's Strict Mode clause, but other claimed clauses are also unscored or not practised. (a) loading-and-error-states#o2, 'handle aborted and malformed requests separately': malformed responses appear nowhere in the starter or tests, and ignoring the AbortError (use-fetch.js lines 11-13) is never asserted, because t6 only checks signal.aborted at lines 21-26 and the tests do not render in Strict Mode. (b) what-makes-a-component-re-render#o3, the only objective claimed for that topic: 'predict which components re-render' is answered for the learner in the TASK 8 comment (StatusLegend.jsx lines 10-16), and 'describe memo as a performance optimisation rather than a correctness fix' is not practised. The task is framed as a fix ('Stop the needless re-render', README line 106), which leans toward the misconception the objective warns against. (c) loading-data-with-useeffect#o2, 'state what an empty array means', is not practised.
findings.recommendation: Extend the partial-objective note to cover these clauses honestly, or add the practice. For example, add one sentence to TASK 8 that memo only skips work and never changes what is shown, and add a t4 case where response.json() rejects (malformed body) that must surface as an error distinct from an HTTP failure.

findings.claim: A 25-minute median and 30-minute cap is not plausible for this task set. Learners build two non-trivial units from blank stubs, useFetch with loading/data/error state, url dependency, reset, AbortController and AbortError filtering, and a full detail page with useParams, useNavigate, four states and five fields. On top of that come a five-route layout tree, NavLink conversion, a four-screen overview refactor, lifting state across two files and memo. That is 8 files across 8 tasks, with cross-task couplings that cost debugging time. The accepted comparable lab (html-css-js/fetch-and-browser-client) budgets 38 minutes median and a 45-minute cap for seven single-function tasks.
findings.recommendation: Cut the task work to fit the 25/30 slot, for example ship the detail page's JSX and have the learner wire only useParams, useFetch and useNavigate, or ship the route tree with only the catch-all and layout missing. Otherwise re-estimate the planning figures and state them in the README as the accepted lab does.

findings.claim: The 'Files you edit' list does not match the TASK markers. It lists starter/src/pages/OverviewPage.jsx for task 6, but TASK 6 part 3 there (lines 23-24) asks for no edit. TASK 6 part 2 has no marker of its own and sits inside the TASK 4 comment in use-fetch.js (line 13). There is a 'TASK 8 (part 2)' marker in OverviewPage.jsx (lines 43-48) that needs no edit, but no 'TASK 8 (part 1)' marker anywhere. The README says 'Every change happens at a TASK n comment', so these labels send learners looking for edits that do not exist.
findings.recommendation: List OverviewPage.jsx for tasks 5 and 7 only. Give task 6 part 2 its own marker in use-fetch.js. Relabel the OverviewPage notes as 'Note (task 6)' and 'Note (task 8)' rather than numbered parts, or add the missing part 1 label in StatusLegend.jsx.

findings.claim: The troubleshooting symptom does not match the cause it names. Fetching a literal '/api/services/:serviceId' does not hang. The ':' fails the mock's id pattern (starter/mock-api.js line 72), so the mock answers 404 'unknown endpoint' at once. With fetchJson fixed, the page shows 'Could not load this service (HTTP 404)', and without the fix it shows an empty service. 'Loading service... forever' comes from a hook that never sets loading to false, not from this mistake.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the entry as 'Every detail page shows HTTP 404 - the URL must include the id from useParams, not a literal :serviceId', and add a separate entry for 'Loading service... forever - check that your hook sets loading to false when the request settles'.

findings.claim: As in part 1, the optional dev block runs 'cd starter' straight after the setup block's 'cd tests' (lines 26-27), with no return to the lab folder, so the command fails from tests/. It also does not mention that 'npm run dev' holds the terminal, so running npm test needs a second terminal.
findings.recommendation: Prefix the block with 'From the lab folder (cd .. if you are still in tests)' and add one line about using a second terminal and stopping the server with Ctrl+C.
